newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst hands RU-486 rights to ex-manager.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst hands RU-486 rights to ex-manager.

text.p: The pharmaceuticals unit of German chemicals group Hoechst AG, Roussel Uclaf, said on Tuesday it was transferring all rights to its controversial abortion pill RU-486 to Edouard Sakiz, a former manager who helped develop the product.
The patent rights for the drug, which has the medical name mifepristone, would be transferred without renumeration to a new company headed by Sakiz, a statement said.
As a result of the transfer, Roussel Uclaf will cease manufacturing, marketing and distribution of the drug.
The pill, which has been strongly opposed by anti-abortionists on the grounds that it gives easy access to abortion, has been a source of image problems for Hoechst for some time.

In a statement, Jean-Pierre Godard, chief executive officer of Roussel Uclaf said that the transfer of rights was part of the general refocusing of Hoechst's total pharmaceutical division Hoechst Marion Roussel.

"This action is part of a continuous process by Hoechst's pharmaceutical division, Hoechst Marion Roussel, to focus its research, development and marketing efforts on those areas that represent the best opportunities to support the company's growth," he said.
